title: Post-rolling update backpressure cascade causing temporary tenant quota collapse
creator: Megan Liu
description:
Summary: After rolling deployment of runtime-2.6.1 to dedicated pools we observed an emergent backpressure feedback loop between the request-side rate limiter and the autoscaler sensor. The interaction produced a cascade where tenant-level burst budgets were depleted faster than expected, autoscaler smoothing suppressed scale-ups for ~6–12 minutes, and the reserved pool headroom calculations failed to account for transiently blocked warmup allocations. Result: ~12 tenants experienced sustained 503 throttles and coldstarts, including a high-usage customer (NovaHealth) who reported degraded SLAs and opened an escalation.

What happened (high level):
- A change in the rate-limiter to aggressively hold connections during transient overloads (patch in runtime-2.6.1) increased the number of in-flight warmup tokens queued at the allocator.
- The autoscaler sensor (windowed 90s smoothing) interpreted the queued latency as transient and suppressed scale-up signals (smoothing algorithm bias towards avoiding oscillation).
- The reserved pool headroom metric used a stale estimate that excluded queued warmup allocations; headroom fell below safety thresholds and burst-credit accounting started returning false positives that allowed tenant requests to consume burst credits rapidly.
- As burst budgets hit zero, tenants were moved to fallback tiers or received 503s; meanwhile the autoscaler remained suppressed for the smoothing window, preventing timely recovery.

Immediate impact:
- Duration: 2026-03-12T14:07Z to 2026-03-12T14:33Z for majority, intermittent aftershocks through 2026-03-12T16:00Z.
- Affected tenants: ~12 dedicated-tenant reservations across us-west-2 and eu-west-1.
- High-profile escalation from NovaHealth (support ticket #NH-8841).

Customer communications:
- 2026-03-12 14:20Z: initial acknowledgement to NovaHealth via SE, we noted degraded performance and that we were investigating.
- 2026-03-12 15:00Z: status update confirming mitigation steps (rollback of limiter patch + emergency extra capacity) and ETA for resolution.
- 2026-03-12 17:10Z: incident summary and follow-up commitment to provide postmortem within 72 hours.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-2.6.1 to a small dedicated pool with two AZs
2) Configure rate-limiter with aggressive hold (new setting introduced in patch: hold_timeout_ms=2000)
3) Generate bursty warmup traffic emulating 40% of pool capacity across 15s intervals for multiple tenants
4) Observe allocator queued warmup tokens, autoscaler sensor smoothing preventing scale-ups, and burst credit exhaustion leading to 503s
mitigation_steps: Hotfix applied (2026-03-12 14:25Z): revert aggressive hold change in rate-limiter (rolled back to hold_timeout_ms=500)
Emergency capacity (2026-03-12 14:27Z): provisioned +2 warm nodes in affected pools via manual override of reserved pool upscaler
Temporary policy (2026-03-12 14:30Z): enabled override to pause autoscaler smoothing for pools exhibiting queued-warmup > 5% of pool size
Customer relief (2026-03-12 14:35Z): restored NovaHealth quota and applied one-time burst-credit compensation while we investigate
timeline_notes: 14:06Z: First alert - multiple 5xx spikes from dedicated pools (pager alerted SRE)
14:12Z: Correlation with runtime-2.6.1 rollout identified; engineers began triage
14:20Z: Hypothesis: new rate-limiter hold change blocking warmups; attempted config tweak in staging
14:25Z: Rollback of limiter patch started; provisioned emergency nodes; customer updated
14:33Z: Error rates dropped to baseline for most tenants; monitoring alerts cleared
15:05Z: Post-rollback validation across regions; scheduled follow-ups and postmortem
root_cause_summary: Combination of an aggressive connection hold introduced in runtime-2.6.1, autoscaler smoothing logic tuned to reduce oscillation, and a reserved-pool headroom calculation that did not include queued warmup allocations. These together allowed queued warmup tokens to silently consume available burst headroom and prevented the autoscaler from issuing timely scale-ups, producing tenant-level capacity starvation.
short_term_followups: 1) Patch autoscaler to add explicit queued-warmup early-exit: treat queued warmup > threshold as immediate scale-up signal (ENG-715010)
2) Change reserved-pool headroom calc to include queued allocations and warmup reservations (ENG-715011)
3) Add a temporary canary gate for future limiter changes that simulates warmup pressure in canary pools before global rollout
4) Create dashboard tile showing queued-warmup per-pool + impact-risk score
long_term_actions: A) Rework autoscaler smoothing to be asymmetric: tolerate transient latency spikes but not queued warmup accumulation (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/d/autoscaler-warmup-smoothing)
B) Build end-to-end test harness that simulates multi-tenant burst scenarios including warmup token churn
C) Formalize customer compensation policy for escalations caused by infrastructure regressions
D) Update runbook to include 'queued warmup' checks and an automated temporary override path for emergency scale-up

notes_for_support: If customers report similar symptoms: 1) collect pool_id, tenant_id, and queued_warmup metric; 2) escalate to SRE with tag 'queued-warmup'; 3) temporarily increase reserved pool capacity or pause limiter hold via emergency override
